subject: science
cluster: Patterns of the sky and seasons
skillName: Patterns of the Sun, Moon, and Stars

items.prompt:
The Sun rises in the
A) east
B) west
C) north
D) ground

steps: The Sun rises in the east each morning.

items.prompt:
The Sun sets in the
A) east
B) west
C) south
D) sky forever

steps: The Sun sets in the west each evening.

items.prompt:
You can usually see stars
A) at night
B) at noon
C) never
D) only in the morning

steps: Stars are usually seen at night.

items.prompt:
The Sun rising and setting gives us
A) day and night
B) rain
C) wind
D) snow

steps: The Sun's pattern gives day and night.

items.prompt:
The Moon's shape seems to change and repeat about every
A) day
B) week
C) month
D) year

steps: The Moon's shape pattern repeats about monthly.

items.prompt:
During the day, the Sun appears to move
A) from west to east
B) from east to west
C) straight up and stay
D) in circles underground

steps: The Sun moves across the sky from east to west.

items.prompt:
We can predict the Sun will rise tomorrow because
A) it rises every morning in a repeating pattern
B) someone turns it on
C) it is random
D) it never rises
items.answer: A) it rises every morning in a repeating pattern

steps: The repeating pattern lets us predict it.

items.prompt:
Why do we see the Sun in the day but stars at night?
A) The Sun is up in the day, and stars show in the dark night sky
B) Stars only exist at noon
C) The Sun shines at night
D) There are no stars
items.answer: A) The Sun is up in the day, and stars show in the dark night sky

steps: The bright Sun is up by day; dim stars show at night.
